items.title: 56422_Leonard Phillips oral history interview
items.q: He was playing alto with his father's band.

ctx.x: So in other words, he switched to tenor when he got in Bronson's because that's what Bronson wanted? He was playing alto right before Bronson, right?

He was playing alto with his father's band. So he left his father's band and went with Bronson. Any time he left his father, his father was taking everything he had. He took all the horns... Let's see, what did he have? He had a clarinet, a baritone and an alto -- those were the instruments -- and a soprano.

items.title: 56422_Leonard Phillips oral history interview
items.q: Sure, everybody. Prez was only about 12 or 13 years old. ... Prez was that far ahead of us. He was already playing.

ctx.x: What school was that? Do you know the name of the school?
It was Myrtle Street School. He got a band together, we started rehearsing -- that was in 1921. Then in 1924, Lester Young's father came to my home town. He had a show there.

items.title: 56422_Leonard Phillips oral history interview
items.q: Cats wasn't blowin' tenor like he was blowin' then.

ctx.x: That's when guys started playing tenors. Ben Webster. Mr. Young taught Ben how to play saxophone. Ben was a piano player. He was playing and violin. Ben said, "I used to hear ole Les in the room, man, playin' that horn, and I'd get in there and try to run over and play, but that cat was gone." But Ben learned fast, you know. He was fooling with alto first, and then he got on tenor, but in a... He stayed with Mr. Young I guess about a year playing piano, and then he was practicing on the saxophone at the same…
He was kind of into Hawkins, wasn't he?
